title: Crisis Access Orchestration and Post-Incident Audit Workflow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and implement an auditable, low-latency emergency access flow (aka break-glass) that integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML, and centralized audit logging. This ticket covers the orchestration of approvals, ephemeral credential issuance, automatic telemetry capture, and a structured post-incident review checklist to ensure we meet compliance and SLOs while minimizing blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: A0: Emergency access can be requested and approved via a one-click flow from the oncall console with MFA + secondary approver when severity is high.
A1: Issued admin credentials are ephemeral (TTL & auto-revoke) and scoped to the minimal set of permissions required by RBAC v2 mappings.

A2: All steps (requestor, approver, justification, issued token id, actions performed) are recorded to the central audit log with immutable identifiers and exported to the audit S3 bucket and SIEM within 5 minutes.
A3: A post-incident wrapper job runs after access revocation to snapshot relevant logs, KV cache state, and active sessions, producing a review artifact and checklist entry in Confluence.
A4: SSO/SAML bypass or assertion elevation is strictly gated and requires automated attestation and a human second factor; no permanent SAML assertions are created.
A5: E2E tests for the flow and log export are added to CI and pass in the nightly security pipeline.
implementation_plan: Design ephemeral credential service extension to RBAC v2: token issuance API, TTL enforcement, permission scoping, and auto-revoke scheduler.
Add a lightweight approval UI in Console -> Oncall Tools with approver hierarchy and 'emergency justification' template.
Wire SAML assertion exchange so that break-glass issuance can perform an SSO-attested elevation with an auditable assertion id.
Integrate with existing audit-logging pipeline: tag records with flow_id, requestor_id, approver_id, token_id, and attach action hashes for verification.
Create CI tests: simulate request -> approve -> perform privileged action -> revoke -> validate logs are present and exported.
Instrument runbooks: add explicit rollback steps and a small command-line helper for SOC to force-revoke tokens and snapshot state.
Coordinate with Legal/Compliance for retention and export requirements and Security for threat modeling of the flow.
Stage rollout behind a feature flag for Dedicated/private customers with audit retention stricter than hosted defaults.
rollout_plan: Alpha: Internal oncall only; flag enabled for 2 weeks; run simulated incidents and collect feedback.
Beta: Security and a set of low-risk internal teams; monitor audit export latency and revoke reliability for 1 sprint.
GA: Enable for all orgs with documentation; publish operational runbook and add to oncall training; enforce mandatory post-access review within 48 hours.
Dedicated/Private: Provide a configuration toggle and KMS/HSM integration guidance; require acceptance test run during deployment.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Elevated credentials could be abused during the granted window. Mitigation: enforce minimal permission scoping, short TTL, continuous watchlist for anomalous commands, and immediate revoke path.
Risk: Audit log ingestion delay resulting in incomplete artifacts. Mitigation: add buffering alerts, fallback export to S3, and end-to-end CI checks with SLAs.
Risk: SSO/SAML bypass accidentally creates persistent assertions. Mitigation: only create transient assertions and validate with SAML logs; require secondary human approver for assertion issuance.
Risk: Oncall confusion or accidental approvals. Mitigation: explicit UX friction (confirmation text, require typed justification), training, and a 'dry-run' mode for low-severity requests.
notes: 2026-02-28: Kickoff with security and oncall; agreed on minimal scope for alpha (request, approve, issue ephemeral token, revoke).
2026-03-04: Design review: decided to reuse RBAC v2 role templates and add 'emergency_scope' claims to tokens.
2026-03-09: UX review: added mandatory 'incident id' field and 2-line justification with a checkbox for post-access review consent.
postmortem_tasks: Automated artifact creation: post-incident job that compiles audit logs, token lifecycle events, screenshots of Console approvals, and attachments into a Confluence page.
Mandatory timeline review within 72 hours with oncall, security lead, and the approver; capture lessons and assign follow-ups.
Rotate any temporary keys discovered during the incident and audit for reuse/permanence risk.
Update RBAC mappings if scope too-broad was used and publish a changelog entry.
